questions.question: The Earth is slightly bulged at:
questions.explanation: Equatorial bulge from rotation.

questions.question: A flat map's main DRAWBACK is:
options: every flat map distorts shapes / sizes / distances
questions.answer: every flat map distorts shapes / sizes / distances
questions.explanation: Projecting a sphere on a plane always distorts.

questions.question: All parallels are:
options: shorter as you go closer to the poles
longer as you go closer to the poles
questions.answer: shorter as you go closer to the poles
questions.explanation: Equator is the longest; parallels shrink towards the poles.

questions.question: The hemisphere ABOVE the equator is called the:
questions.explanation: Above (north of) equator = Northern hemisphere.

questions.question: The hemisphere BELOW the equator is called the:
questions.explanation: Below (south of) equator = Southern hemisphere.

questions.question: Which two countries are partly in the Frigid Zone?
questions.explanation: Both extend north of the Arctic Circle (66½° N).

questions.question: The hemisphere EAST of the Prime Meridian is called the:
questions.explanation: By convention.

questions.question: The hemisphere WEST of the Prime Meridian is called the:
questions.explanation: By convention.

questions.question: London is at approximately (51.5° N, 0.1° W). London is in which hemispheres?
questions.explanation: 51.5° N → Northern; 0.1° W → just inside the Western hemisphere.

questions.question: Tokyo is at approximately (35.7° N, 139.7° E). Tokyo is in which heat zone?
questions.explanation: 35.7° N is between 23½° N and 66½° N — north temperate.

questions.question: If two cities are 60° of longitude apart, the time difference between them is:
When it is 6 pm in Mumbai (75° E), what time is it in London (0°)?
questions.explanation: 75° east → 75/15 = 5 hours ahead. So Mumbai = London + 5 h. London = Mumbai − 5 h = 6 pm − 5 h = 1 pm. (Approximate; actual depends on whether London uses GMT or BST.) Closest option: 1 pm. The 12:30 pm option corresponds to using exactly 75° vs IST 82.5° E. Choose the listed answer that fits — 1 pm is the standard textbook answer.

questions.question: Place X is at the equator on the Prime Meridian (0°, 0°). Place Y is at the North Pole (90° N). Which is correct?
options: they are at the same latitude
they are at the same longitude
questions.explanation: 90° N is the maximum north.

questions.question: Going from the equator to the pole, the latitude value INCREASES.
questions.explanation: 0° at equator → 90° at pole.

questions.question: All meridians are circles around the Earth.
questions.explanation: Each meridian is a HALF-circle (semicircle) from pole to pole; together with its opposite meridian it forms a great circle.

questions.question: The Earth turns 1° in 4 minutes.
questions.explanation: 60 minutes / 15° = 4 minutes per degree.

questions.question: The Tropic of Cancer passes through ____.
questions.explanation: Tropic of Cancer (23½° N) passes through central India.

questions.question: Two places at the same latitude are at the same distance from the ____.
questions.explanation: Latitude measures distance north / south of equator.

questions.question: Write the latitude of: (a) the equator, (b) the Tropic of Cancer, (c) the Arctic Circle, (d) the North Pole.
questions.answer: (a) Equator: 0°. (b) Tropic of Cancer: 23½° N. (c) Arctic Circle: 66½° N. (d) North Pole: 90° N.
questions.explanation: Recall of named parallels.

questions.question: Which city has these approximate coordinates: (a) (28.6° N, 77.2° E)? (b) (51.5° N, 0.1° W)? (c) (33.9° S, 151.2° E)?
questions.explanation: Standard examples from major world cities.

questions.question: Two cities are 45° apart in longitude. Compute the time difference between them and explain.
questions.answer: Time difference = 45 ÷ 15 = 3 hours. Reason: the Earth turns 360° in 24 hours, which is 15° per hour. So 45° corresponds to 45/15 = 3 hours.
questions.explanation: Apply the 15°-per-hour rule.

questions.question: Two students are studying weather. Student A lives at 5° N (near the equator). Student B lives at 60° N (in northern Europe). Use the heat-zone idea to predict (i) which student has hotter weather year-round, (ii) which student has more dramatic seasons (winter vs summer), and (iii) why.
questions.answer: (i) Student A (5° N) has hotter weather year-round, because they live in the TORRID Zone where the sun is nearly overhead twice a year and sunlight is concentrated. (ii) Student B (60° N) has more dramatic seasons, because they live in the temperate / sub-arctic zone where the Earth's tilt creates very different sun-angles between summer and winter. (iii) The sun's angle determines heat — a high (overhead) sun spreads its energy over a small patch of ground (intense heat); a low (slanting) sun spreads the same energy over a much larger patch (less intense heat). Near the equator the sun stays high all year; far north or south, the sun's height changes a lot between summer and winter.
questions.explanation: Connects latitude → heat zone → climate experience.
